title: nf-prime-ideals
objective: Implement certified rational-prime decomposition, prime ideals, ideal inversion, valuations, and factorization internals.

handoff.summary: Implemented an exact Project-2 vertical slice in two strict lazy modules: NumberFieldPrimeIdeal and Sage-style certified decompositions; gated Dedekind--Kummer using the integral equation generator; a presentation-independent O/pO fallback using Frobenius nilradicals and recursive Frobenius-fixed component splitting (including nonmonogenic F_2^3); independent quotient-field, residue-map, comaximality, degree, and exact HNF-product verification; residue fields/maps, uniformizers, serialization authentication, cache and compact prime-range streams; plus exact colon, inverse, quotient, negative powers, denominators, containment/divisibility, element/ideal valuations, and reconstructing integral-ideal factorization. Runtime differential checks covered inert/split/ramified/wild/index-dividing primes, the Dedekind nonmonogenic cubic, degrees 2--4, fast/fallback agreement, exact inverses and valuations, serialization, streams, and p=1099511627791.
risks: Integration must add thin NumberFieldParent/NumberFieldOrder/NumberFieldIdeal methods and register both lazy modules for strict/precompiled builds; those shared files were outside this lane's claims.
The explicit supported domain is degree <= 16, p <= 2^53-1, 4096 primitive candidates per residue field, and prime-stream intervals of length <= 1000000.

Serialization includes exact field/order fingerprints and live identity tokens; it intentionally rejects reconstruction in a distinct isomorphic-looking field instance until an explicit transport-map contract exists.
No native boundary changed, so pnpm test:native and four-platform integration smoke tests remain for the integration lane.
next_steps: Bind factor_rational_prime, primes_above, splitting_records, inverse, quotient, valuation, factor, and serialization through thin public bootstrap methods.
Add the modules to pyrightconfig.json and scripts/precompiled-python-packages.json, then add focused public tests using the committed number-field oracle corpus.
Run pnpm architecture:check, the public number-field suites, and Linux arm64/macOS arm64/Windows x64 smoke tests after integration.
